parts.text: the change kind heading, quoted from the Changelog (one of the words the Changelog itself uses: Added, Changed, Fixed, Removed, Deprecated, Security)

notes: The phrase fact carries the six page words the look lists as a single phrase fact: the quote must say ONE of "Added", "Changed", "Fixed", "Removed", "Deprecated", "Security", copied exactly from the Changelog. I used the input's own words from the look rather than the person's wording.
Line 1's ~ rules 1 ("exactly 3 bullets") and 2 ("under 80 words") are settled by code: code writes the list-item and word-count checks itself, so no part and no refused entry are written for them.
"Summarise the latest release" — which release counts as the latest, and whether the summary is a fair or accurate summary of it, needs reading the text to judge; nothing checks it.
The release version and the release date cannot be quoted as facts: the Changelog holds no label for either (the look lists both under NOT CHECKED), so they are left to code's Not checked list.

parts.text: the release version and date, quoted from the Changelog exactly as it writes it

notes: Line 1 is a writing line (a summary), so the word and list-item limits are settled by code: line 1 ~ rule 1 (exactly 3 bullets) and ~ rule 2 (under 80 words) get no part and no refused entry from me.

The phrase fact uses the input's own words: the look gives three acceptable page words, and I picked the versioned one the confirmed plan named, "## [0.54.1] - 2026-11-04" (the other two are "## [Unreleased]" and "## [0.54.0] - 2026-11-03").

refused.reason: which release is the "latest release" — the choice of which one is the newest cannot be judged by a check
that the bullets are a correct and faithful summary of the release — accuracy and quality of the summary would need a person to read the text
